implement.approach: Rebuilt from BASE_SHA 7cfeacbb: (1) 6851450b re-applies the sound r4 module (canonical native/vision-core/Sources/OfflineWallet.swift symlinked into LocalPods/PickleNative/Sources/Core, PickleOfflineWallet.swift RN wrapper on a serial queue, PickleOfflineWalletBridge.m, podspec hunk, typed TS bridge). (2) f4437ea8 adds 8 regression tests (fail on r4). (3) a9d3683e hardens the core: fence payload gains `epoch` (16 random bytes, hex) and `cleared`; every wallet envelope carries the epoch and a `cleared` flag. clear() is fence-first — CAS fence to {revision N, cleared:true} then CAS the wallet item to an HMAC-sealed cleared envelope at N (tombstone) — so the removed envelope at N, whether replayed after a completed clear, after a lagging-fence repair, or left behind by a crash between the two writes, fails as `tampered` ('rolled back'); the next replace mints max(stored, fence)+1. load() reports a missing wallet item beside a fence >= 1 as `tampered` ('missing'), and a payload whose epoch differs from the fence epoch as `tampered`. discardCorrupt over a verified fence rotates the epoch (revision kept, cleared, tombstone written) so envelopes the fence never recorded also die; with no verifiable fence it deletes wallet, integrity key and fence (history cannot be carried forward, so the key that verifies old envelopes is retired). replace() reuses a key only together with its fence; a key with no fence is replaced (CAS on the old key bytes). commitFence tolerates an already-advanced same-epoch fence. Bridge codes/TS contract unchanged. (4) The remote branch already contained the r4 history, integrated with `merge -s ours` (no force-push).

Semantics deliberately changed vs r4, which 4 adversary testAttack_* assertions (attack-6cdd3ab9 branch) still pin: (a) OfflineWalletAttackTests.swift:271 expects an interrupted clear (fence committed, wallet not yet replaced) to leave the old wallet readable — that state is byte-identical to the P1 #1b replay the same suite requires to be `tampered`, so it now reads `tampered` and recovers via discardCorrupt; (b) :236 'exactly one key per owner' after a crash following the key write — indistinguishable from the P2 #2a fence-loss scenario (:124) that demands a fresh key, so a key without a fence is now replaced (2 key writes); (c) :327 expects 5 items after B's clear and (d) :388 expects the wallet item gone after discardCorrupt — clear/discard now leave an authenticated cleared envelope (tombstone) at the retired revision so 'cleared at N' is distinguishable from 'wallet missing at N' (P3). The security properties those tests guard (owner isolation, typed unreadable failures, no altered contents ever read, committed receipts survive crashes, revisions strictly upward) all still hold in the runs; only the mechanism assertions differ.

Two existing r4 test expectations in the write path were inverted to match the hardened design (documented, not weakened): testCrashBetweenKeyMintAndWalletWriteRecovers now asserts an orphaned key is replaced (was: reused) and testMissingOrCorruptFenceBesideAWalletIsTamperedAndDiscardable asserts the key leaves with an unverifiable fence (was: stays); testMissingIntegrityKey... asserts a cleared envelope without its key is `integrity_key_missing` (was: nil).

Recovery cost: an interrupted clear, a vanished wallet item, or a lost/corrupt fence now require the owner to reconcile with the server and call discardCorrupt before the wallet is writable again (by design: ambiguous state => HOLD, never fabricated empty history).
Whole-store rollback (key + fence + wallet restored together from an older backup) remains undetectable by construction, as in r3/r4.
